statement.p: Let f(x)=\frac{1}{s\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-\frac{(x-m)^2}{2s^2}} on (-\infty,\infty)\text{,} where s>0 and m are constants. Find the minimum and maximum values of f(x)\text{,} if they exist.

Which statement about the minimum value is correct?
A minimum value exists and is 0.
No minimum value exists.
A minimum value exists at x=m.
Maximum value:

solution.p: \frac{1}{s\sqrt{2\pi}} is a constant. The derivative of e^{-\frac{(x-m)^2}{2s^2}} is
Setting this equal to zero, we find the critical point x=m\text{.}
Plugging in give \displaystyle f(m) = \frac{1}{s\sqrt{2\pi}}\text{.} This is the maximum value.
As x\to\infty or x\to -\infty\text{,} the function approaches 0\text{,} but it never equals 0\text{.} Therefore, no minimum value exists.
